sources.citation: Meira, Sérgio. 2006. Cariban languages. In Keith Brown (ed.), Encyclopedia of Language & Linguistics, 2nd edition, vol. 2, 199-203. Oxford: Elsevier.
sources.note: Phonology paragraph (p. 201) is family-level only: 'Many languages have weight-sensitive rhythmic (iambic) stress (Table 1; Meira, 1998); some, however, have simple cumulative, usually penultimate, stress (Panare, Bakairi, Kuikuro, Yukpa).' Table 1 illustrates Tiriyo. Nothing on Tiverighotto; no tone/stress statement attributable to this languoid.

sources.citation: Gildea, Spike. 2003. Proposing a new branch for the Cariban language family. Amerindia 28: 7-32. Paris: A.E.A.
sources.note: Nothing for Tiverikoto. The paper is a classification/branch proposal (Venezuelan branch: Panare, Pemon and Mapoyo-Tamanaku groups). Tiverikoto (extinct, marked with a dagger) appears by name only in two reproduced classifications: Girard (1971) Fig. 1 group 4 'Wayana' (p. 9) and Kaufman (1994) Fig. 3 'K. Yao Group: Tiverikoto, Yao' (p. 12). The only prosodic remark in the whole paper is generic, p. 9, about early wordlist sources: 'I add (Gildea 1998a: 10) that most sources have been unable to reliably indicate stress. All of these flaws are found in most wordlists for most Cariban languages…
